scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original A2 independent assessment draft with ten new inference, argument or transfer questions. Content requires teacher approval.

tabs.title: Useful Study Habits
tabs.description: Use Daniel's ideas in everyday learning.

questions.q: Why does Daniel put a study plan above his desk?
choices: He wants to prepare in a different, calmer way.
He needs to remember where his desk is.
He has to show his sister his test mark.
He wants to stop studying for science.
questions.explanation: Daniel wants to avoid the tiring routine of studying everything the night before.

questions.q: What does Daniel discover when he cannot explain an idea to his sister?
choices: He should change the subject of the test.
He needs to check and understand it better.
His sister has already learnt everything.
He should stop practising questions.
questions.explanation: Not being able to explain an idea shows a gap, so he goes back to his notes.

questions.q: Why is the test not a complete success?
choices: He forgets to bring his notes to school.
He does not sit the science test.
Daniel still answers two questions incorrectly.
He goes to sleep too early.
questions.explanation: The third paragraph makes it clear that Daniel still makes two mistakes.

questions.q: How does Daniel's Wednesday change in the new plan?
choices: He studies for three hours without a break.
He spends the entire evening doing the test.
He asks his sister to answer every question.
He studies without phone notifications and has a calmer evening.
questions.explanation: Daniel turns off notifications and is happy that he can enjoy Wednesday evening.

questions.q: Why is Daniel happy even though the mark is not perfect?
choices: His teacher has cancelled the next test.
He feels rested and knows how to improve.
He has finished studying every subject.
He no longer needs to revise for history.
questions.explanation: The last paragraph values calmness and sleep as well as a slightly improved mark.

questions.q: What will Daniel do before his history test?
choices: Study only on the evening before.
Ask his sister not to help him.
Follow the exact plan even if it fails.
Use the plan again, changing it if needed.
questions.explanation: He intends to try the same approach for history and adapt it when necessary.

questions.q: Ella reads her notes for hours but forgets the facts. Which idea from Daniel's plan could help?
choices: Try questions without looking at the answers.
Wait until the night before the test.
Read notes but never take a break.
Keep all phone notifications on.
questions.explanation: Trying questions without answers is part of Daniel's more active study plan.

questions.q: You cannot explain a science idea to a friend. What is a useful next step?
choices: Pretend that you understand everything.
Stop asking your friend questions.
Check your notes and try to explain it again.
Write a new study timetable only.
questions.explanation: Daniel learns from being unable to explain an idea and checks his notes.

questions.q: What might Daniel say to someone who wants to study all night?
choices: A good mark means you never need sleep.
Short sessions and enough rest may work better.
Every subject should be studied for three hours at once.
Studying longer always helps you remember more.
questions.explanation: His earlier late-night approach made him tired, whereas the new one includes breaks and sleep.

questions.q: A test result shows you missed one topic. Which response fits Daniel's example?
choices: Ignore the result because one mark is enough.
Give up on the topic that caused a mistake.
Study exactly the same way without checking why.
Write down what you need to practise next.
questions.explanation: After the science test Daniel records what still needs practice instead of giving up.
